summary: 41 display-math items enumerated in order of appearance (26 labelled equations, 15 unlabelled displays, two of which are align blocks split into sub-items). No discrepancies found: every stated identity in ch03 checks out. 26 proved, 15 defined, 0 instance_checked, 0 skipped. (2026-09-14: the last two instance_checked items, eq:ar1-toeplitz and eq:dev-fisher-zero, were generalised and are now proved from the model rather than from assumed second-moment recursions or an alpha-free density.)

items.summary: Strict stationarity: all finite-dimensional laws invariant under a time shift.
items.note: Definition, not a claim. Encoded as equality of push-forward measures of the finite-dimensional coordinate maps, for every n, every index tuple and every shift h. Sanity lemma proved: a strictly stationary process re-indexed by a constant shift is again strictly stationary.

items.summary: Constant mean E[X_k] = mu, first half of weak stationarity.
items.note: Definition. Folded into the ch03_WeaklyStationary predicate as the clause forall k, integral of X k = m.

items.summary: Cov(X_j, X_k) = gamma(j-k), second half of weak stationarity.
items.note: Definition. Sanity lemma PROVED: weak stationarity forces gamma(-d) = gamma(d), which is exactly the fact the chapter invokes at line 56 to fill in the Toeplitz matrix of eq:toeplitz.

items.summary: Sigma_ij = gamma(i-j) is Toeplitz: constant along every diagonal, and symmetric when gamma is even.
items.note: Three theorems: (i) entries with equal i-j agree, for arbitrary L; (ii) the matrix is symmetric given gamma(-d)=gamma(d); (iii) the explicit 4x4 block displayed in the chapter is reproduced entry by entry. Displayed entries are correct.
Definition. Encoded in density form: the conditional density c n x of x_{n+1} given the whole past x_0..x_n equals K (x n) (x (n+1)). Its content is discharged by eq:chain-factorisation below.

PROVED by induction from the chain rule (ch03_joint) plus the Markov property: ch03_joint p0 c x m = p0 (x 0) * prod over Finset.range m of K (x k) (x (k+1)). With m = L-1 this is exactly the displayed product over k = 0..L-2, so the index range in the display is correct.

items.summary: a_{k+1} = alpha a_k + eta_k, eta_k iid N(0, q).
items.note: Definition (the recursion). Sanity lemma proved: with the innovations switched off the solution is a_k = alpha^k a_0, the geometric contraction.

items.lean_name: ch03_AR1, ch03_ar1_cov_step_proc, ch03_ar1_var_step_proc, ch03_ar1_toeplitz_proc, ch03_ar1_toeplitz_matrix_proc, ch03_ar1_lin, ch03_ar1_drive, ch03_ar1_state_eq_lin, ch03_ar1_indep_of_iIndepFun, ch03_ar1_toeplitz_of_iIndepFun, ch03_ar1_state_law, ch03_AR1_of_drive, ch03_AR1_exists, ch03_ar1_toeplitz, ch03_ar1_cov, ch03_ar1_is_toeplitz, ch03_ar1_toeplitz_display
items.summary: Cov(a_j,a_k) = alpha^{|j-k|} for the stationary AR(1) chain, giving the displayed Toeplitz Sigma.
items.note: PROVED IN GENERAL (2026-09-14 pass), at arbitrary index pairs and arbitrary length L. The structure `ch03_AR1 alpha a eta mu` states the model of eq:ar1 as hypotheses on a real family of random variables on an arbitrary probability space: square-integrability, the PATHWISE recursion a_{k+1} omega = alpha * a_k omega + eta_k omega, independence of each innovation from the states it has not yet influenced, Var(a_0) = 1 and Var(eta_k) = q = 1 - alpha^2 (the choice of line 99). From these alone: ch03_ar1_cov_step_proc derives Cov(a_j, a_{k+1}) = alpha Cov(a_j, a_k) by bilinearity of mathlib's `covariance` plus IndepFun.covariance_eq_zero, and ch03_ar1_var_step_proc derives Var(a_{k+1}) = alpha^2 Var(a_k) + (1 - alpha^2). Feeding those into the pre-existing uniqueness theorem ch03_ar1_toeplitz gives ch03_ar1_toeplitz_proc: cov[a j, a k; mu] = alpha^{|j-k|} for all j, k; ch03_ar1_toeplitz_matrix_proc gives the displayed matrix Sigma = ch03_toeplitz L (alpha^{|d|}) at every L. The independence clause is itself derived, not assumed: ch03_ar1_state_eq_lin solves eq:ar1 as a_m = ch03_ar1_lin alpha m (a_0, eta_0, ..., eta_{m-1}), a fixed affine function of the first m+1 coordinates of the driving vector, and ch03_ar1_indep_of_iIndepFun then gets IndepFun (a j) (eta k) for j <= k out of iIndepFun of the driving vector via iIndepFun.indepFun_finset + IndepFun.comp. ch03_ar1_toeplitz_of_iIndepFun is the end-to-end statement from the primitive hypotheses only (recursion + joint independence of (a_0, eta_0, eta_1, ...) + the two variances). NON-VACUITY: ch03_AR1_exists shows that for every alpha with alpha^2 <= 1 -- exactly the range in which q = 1 - alpha^2 is a variance -- a process satisfying every clause exists (built from ProbabilityTheory.exists_iid), its states are genuinely N(0,1) (ch03_ar1_state_law, the prose claim of lines 99-100, proved by induction with gaussianReal_add_gaussianReal_of_indepFun), and its covariance is alpha^{|j-k|}. HONEST RESIDUE: ch03_AR1 encodes the model at the level of second moments only, so the covariance theorem never uses Gaussianity (Gaussianity is used only in ch03_ar1_state_law / ch03_AR1_exists); 'eta_k iid and independent of a_0' is encoded as joint independence of the driving vector (a_0, eta_0, eta_1, ...), which is what iid-plus-independent-initialisation means. [HISTORY] recorded 'proved' initially; downgraded to instance_checked on 2026-09-13 because the then-current ch03_ar1_toeplitz assumed the two second-moment recursions rather than deriving them from eq:ar1, and the displayed matrix was only checked at L = 5. Both gaps are now closed.

items.summary: dX_t = -X_t dt + sqrt(2) dW_t, X_0 = a.
items.note: An SDE; stochastic calculus is out of reach here. Its deterministic part is checked: a e^{-t} solves x' = -x with x(0) = a (HasDerivAt statement), i.e. the contraction factor e^{-t} of eq:ou-channel is the right one for this drift. Note the variance-preserving normalisation is consistent: drift -1 and diffusion sqrt(2) give stationary variance 2/(2*1) = 1, matching N(0,1) as the invariant law claimed at line 149.

items.summary: d(e^t X_t) = e^t X_t dt + e^t dX_t = sqrt(2) e^t dW_t: the drift cancels exactly.
items.note: PROVED in three pieces: the ordinary product rule d/dt (e^t X_t) = e^t X_t + e^t X'_t as a HasDerivAt statement (justifying the chapter's remark that no Ito correction appears, since e^t carries no stochastic part); the displayed algebraic cancellation e^t X dt + e^t(-X dt + sqrt2 dW) = sqrt2 e^t dW; and the corollary that in the noiseless case e^t X_t has derivative 0.

items.summary: e^t X_t - a = I_t  ==>  X_t = a e^{-t} + e^{-t} I_t.
items.note: PROVED (division by the nonvanishing e^t).

PROVED. The integral is computed by the fundamental theorem of calculus (antiderivative e^{2s}/2) giving (e^{2t}-1)/2, and the final chain 2e^{-2t}(e^{2t}-1)/2 = 1-e^{-2t} is closed by linear_combination on e^{-2t}e^{2t}=1. Both displayed equalities are correct.

items.summary: X_t | X_0 = a ~ N(a e^{-t}, Delta_t), Delta_t = 1 - e^{-2t}.
items.note: PROVED at the level of laws using Mathlib's gaussianReal: if eps has law N(0,1) then a e^{-t} + sqrt(Delta_t) eps has law N(a e^{-t}, Delta_t). Uses gaussianReal_map_const_mul and gaussianReal_map_const_add plus (sqrt Delta)^2 = Delta.

items.summary: x = a e^{-t} + sqrt(Delta_t) eps, eps ~ N(0,1): signal contracted by e^{-t}, noise of variance Delta_t added.
items.note: PROVED: the law statement (same theorem as noname-5), plus the properties the surrounding prose asserts - at t = 0 the channel is the identity (Delta_0 = 0, e^{-0} = 1, so x = a), Delta_t is nondecreasing in t, and 0 <= Delta_t < 1 for t >= 0.

items.lean_name: ch03_IsPropagator, ch03_IsPropagator_id, ch03_margScoreFamily, ch03_margScoreFamily_apply, ch03_dev_propagator_marginal_none, ch03_jointScoreFamily, ch03_jointScoreFamily_apply, ch03_dev_propagator_gaussian_none, ch03_dev_propagator_joint_none, ch03_dev_L2_precision_isUnit
items.summary: S_{:,u}(x) ~= P_t(S_{:,u-1}(x)): the conjectured score propagator. The display is a HYPOTHESIS the chapter states and then rejects, not an identity it asserts; what is proved here is the chapter's verdict on it, that no such P_t exists.
items.note:
PROVED (was: skipped). Read carefully: 'proved' means the REFUTATION is proved, not that the displayed relation holds. The display is first given definite content - ch03_IsPropagator s P says s_u(x) = P (s_{u-1}(x)) exactly, for every pair of consecutive frames and every trajectory, with frame blocks scalar as they are for this chapter's scalar chains. P_t is allowed to be a completely ARBITRARY function R -> R: no linearity, continuity or measurability is assumed, so the non-existence results are the strongest form of the negative statement and are not artefacts of a restricted search space. ch03_IsPropagator_id shows the predicate is satisfiable (a family whose block does not depend on the frame index is propagated by the identity), so the non-existence theorems are not vacuous. (i) ch03_dev_propagator_marginal_none: for every length L >= 2 and every P, the per-frame MARGINAL score family - the object the six toy models of sec 3.3 computed, which by noname-13 is x |-> -x_u at every frame for every alpha and every t - admits no propagator. This is exactly the chapter's own verdict at lines 254-258 ('no propagator could have been found in it: there was nothing left for P_t to propagate'): the block at frame u-1 sees only x_{u-1}, so two trajectories agreeing at frame u-1 and differing at frame u force P_t to take two values at one argument. (ii) ch03_dev_propagator_joint_none: the JOINT score of a nondegenerate centred Gaussian trajectory, s_t(x) = -Sigma_t^{-1} x, admits no pointwise propagator either, for any n >= 2 and any invertible symmetric precision matrix; witnesses x = 0 and x = S^{-1} e_k agree in coordinate j of Sx and differ in coordinate k. ch03_dev_L2_precision_isUnit checks the invertibility hypothesis is met by the chapter's own two-frame Sigma_t^{-1}, so (ii) is not vacuous. SCOPE LIMIT, stated explicitly: (ii) goes beyond what the chapter claims, and it refutes only the pointwise, frame-local operator that eq:dev-propagator literally writes - one that reconstructs the block at frame u from the value of the block at frame u-1 alone. It says nothing about operators acting on the whole score vector, on several past blocks, or on the score as a function.

[FIDELITY NOTE 2026-09-13] Status kept as 'proved', but note what is proved: this display is the chapter's REJECTED conjecture S_{:,u}(x) ~~ P_t(S_{:,u-1}(x)), and the Lean proves its negation in an exact form -- ch03_IsPropagator is defined with exact equality, and is shown unsatisfiable for the marginal and joint score families. So the chapter's negative verdict is verified; the display is not a verified identity, and refuting exact propagation does not refute the approximate ('~~') conjecture the chapter actually wrote. Readers counting 'proved' items should exclude this one from the count of verified identities.

items.summary: s(x_u,u,t) = grad_{x_u} log p_t(x_u | u), the per-frame marginal score.
items.note: Definition, encoded as the derivative of the log of the one-frame density.

items.summary: S_k(x,t) = (e^{-t} E[a_k | x_0..x_{L-1}] - x_k)/Delta_t (Tweedie for the joint score).
items.note: PROVED in the Gaussian setting in full generality in n. Hypotheses: Sigma_t = e^{-2t} Sigma_0 + Delta_t I, Delta_t != 0, y = Sigma_t^{-1} x (encoded as Sigma_t y = x), and the Gaussian posterior mean E[a|x] = e^{-t} Sigma_0 Sigma_t^{-1} x. Conclusion: (e^{-t}(e^{-t}(Sigma_0 y)_k) - x_k)/Delta_t = -y_k, i.e. the right-hand side of the display collapses to -(Sigma_t^{-1}x)_k, which is the joint score of eq:dev-general-gaussian. The two formulas are therefore consistent.

items.summary: s_t(x) = grad_x log p_t(x_0,...,x_{L-1}), the joint score.
items.note: Definition, encoded componentwise as the partial derivative in coordinate k via Function.update. It is this definition that noname-12a/b and eq:dev-general-gaussian are proved against.

items.note: Definition. Its type, R -> R, is the formal content of the boxed claim eq:dev-joint-vs-marginal that a marginal score 'cannot' depend on the other frames.

items.summary: Boxed: the joint score component k may depend on the other frames, the marginal score cannot.
items.note: PROVED in the only direction with content. The 'cannot' half is a typing fact (ch03_dev_marg_score_block is a function of x_k alone). The 'may' half is an existence statement, proved: for r != 0 and 1-r^2 != 0 the map x_1 |-> -(x_0 - r x_1)/(1-r^2) is non-constant (witnesses x_0 = 0, x_1 = 0 vs x_1' = 1, values 0 vs r/(1-r^2) != 0).

items.summary: Boxed: Sigma_t = e^{-2t} Sigma_0 + Delta_t I, (Sigma_0)_{ij} = alpha^{|i-j|}, s_t(x) = -Sigma_t^{-1} x.
items.note: PROVED in general n. The first two clauses are definitions (ch03_Sigmat, ch03_Sigma0), checked against eq:ar1-toeplitz. The third is a theorem: for any symmetric precision matrix S, the k-th partial derivative of the centred Gaussian log-density C - (1/2) x^T S x is -(S x)_k. The computational core (ch03_quadform_hasDerivAt) is the derivative of a symmetric quadratic form in one coordinate, proved for arbitrary n, giving 2 (S x)_k.

items.summary: (Sigma_t)_{ij} = 1 for i = j, e^{-2t} alpha^{|i-j|} for i != j.
items.note: PROVED from Sigma_t = e^{-2t} Sigma_0 + Delta_t I: the diagonal is e^{-2t} * alpha^0 + (1 - e^{-2t}) = 1, the off-diagonal is e^{-2t} alpha^{|i-j|}. The chapter's conclusion that the diagonal - hence every one-frame marginal - is independent of alpha is therefore correct.

items.lean_name: ch03_Sigma0_diag, ch03_ou_frame_law, ch03_onemarginal_pdf, ch03_onemarginal_pdf_eq, ch03_onemarginal_pdf_const, ch03_onemarginal_pdf_rnDeriv, ch03_onemarginal_law_indep_of_alpha, ch03_dev_fisher_zero_deriv, ch03_dev_fisher_zero, ch03_dev_fisher_zero_law
items.summary: d/d alpha log p_{t,k} = 0, hence I_k(alpha) = E[(d/d alpha log p_{t,k})^2] = 0.
items.note: PROVED IN GENERAL (2026-09-14 pass). The one-frame density is no longer a lambda that ignores its alpha argument: ch03_onemarginal_pdf alpha t L k x is defined as mathlib's gaussianPDFReal 0 ((Sigma_t)_{kk}).toNNReal x, i.e. the centred Gaussian density whose variance is read off the model's own Sigma_t = e^{-2t} Sigma_0 + Delta_t I with (Sigma_0)_{ij} = alpha^{|i-j|}. alpha therefore occurs in the differentiated function. ch03_onemarginal_pdf_eq then PROVES it equals (2 pi)^{-1/2} e^{-x^2/2} for every alpha, t, L and frame k, because (Sigma_0)_{kk} = alpha^0 = 1 (ch03_Sigma0_diag) and e^{-2t} + Delta_t = 1. ch03_dev_fisher_zero_deriv differentiates that genuine function of alpha and gets 0; ch03_dev_fisher_zero gives the boxed I_k(alpha) = 0 for an arbitrary observation X on an arbitrary measure space, and ch03_dev_fisher_zero_law specialises it to the frame's own law. The thesis's PREMISE -- that the corrupted one-frame law carries no alpha -- is also proved, at the level of laws rather than assumed: ch03_ou_frame_law shows that if frame k of the clean chain has the stationary marginal N(0, (Sigma_0)_{kk}) and the OU channel adds sqrt(Delta_t) times an independent standard normal, then X_k = e^{-t} a_k + sqrt(Delta_t) Z has law N(0,1) for every alpha and every t >= 0 (via gaussianReal_map_const_mul and gaussianReal_add_gaussianReal_of_indepFun); ch03_onemarginal_pdf_rnDeriv confirms ch03_onemarginal_pdf is that law's density (rnDeriv against Lebesgue), and ch03_onemarginal_law_indep_of_alpha states the law-level alpha-independence. HONEST RESIDUE: ch03_ou_frame_law takes the Gaussianity of the clean frame as model input (its variance value (Sigma_0)_{kk} is the content of eq:ar1-toeplitz, proved separately); mathlib has no general Fisher-information definition, so I_k(alpha) is written out as the integral of the squared alpha-score, which is the display's own definition. Once the score vanishes the integral is trivially zero -- that is the thesis's own argument, and the non-trivial half (the score vanishes) is what is now proved. [HISTORY] recorded 'proved' initially; downgraded to instance_checked on 2026-09-13 because both lemmas differentiated a lambda that ignored its alpha argument by construction, so the boxed claim's whole content was built in. That gap is now closed.

items.summary: X_t = e^{-t} A + sqrt(Delta_t) Z  ==>  phi_{X_t}(u) = phi_A(e^{-t} u) exp(-Delta_t u^2/2).
items.note: PROVED measure-theoretically with Mathlib's charFun: independence of the two summands turns the characteristic function of the sum into the product; charFun_map_mul_comp rescales the argument of phi_A to e^{-t} u; and charFun_gaussianReal gives exp(-Delta_t u^2/2) for the sqrt(Delta_t)-scaled standard Gaussian. Also PROVED: the specialisation at line 470 - if A ~ N(0,1) the two Gaussian factors combine to e^{-u^2/2} exactly.

items.summary: For unit-variance Laplace data, phi_{X_t}(u) = exp[-Delta_t u^2/2] / (1 + e^{-2t} u^2/2).
items.note: PROVED, and the Laplace characteristic function is now COMPUTED rather than assumed (this closes the gap the previous note recorded). ch03_noname_14 substitutes phi_A(v) = (1 + v^2/2)^{-1} into eq:dev-cf at v = e^{-t} u and gets (1 + e^{-2t} u^2/2)^{-1}, so the display is correct. The input phi_A is no longer a hypothesis: ch03_laplace_density b y = (2b)^{-1} e^{-|y|/b} is the scale-b Laplace density; ch03_laplace_density_integral_one proves it integrates to 1, so it is a genuine probability density; ch03_laplace_variance proves its variance is 2b^2, by reflection at 0 and the Gamma integral (Gamma(3) = 2), which together with ch03_laplace_unit_variance is what forces b = 1/sqrt(2) for unit variance - previously only the arithmetic 2b^2 = 1 was checked; and ch03_laplace_charFun proves int_R e^{iuy} (2b)^{-1} e^{-|y|/b} dy = (1 + b^2 u^2)^{-1} from the definition, by splitting R at 0 and evaluating the two one-sided complex exponential integrals (integral_exp_mul_complex_Iic / _Ioi). ch03_laplace_unit_charFun specialises to b = 1/sqrt(2), giving exactly (1 + u^2/2)^{-1}, the value the chapter states at line 472; ch03_noname_14_laplace is noname-14 with that value substituted, i.e. with the hypothesis hphi discharged. Presentational caveat: the characteristic function is stated as the Lebesgue integral of e^{iuy} against the density, not as Mathlib's charFun of a constructed measure.

items.note: PROVED: with psi_C = exp(-E_C) the product of exponentials is the exponential of the sum of the negated energies. (The Hammersley-Clifford equivalence with conditional independence is a cited theorem, not a display-math identity; only the displayed equality of the two factorised forms is checked here.)

items.lean_name: ch03_bp_var_to_fac, ch03_bp_fac_to_var, ch03_bp_belief, ch03_bp_leaf_message, ch03_bp_exact_two, ch03_bp_exact_three
items.summary: Sum-product updates: nu_{i->a} proportional to prod over b in di\a of nuhat_{b->i}; nuhat_{a->i} proportional to the factor integrated against the other incoming variable messages.
items.note: Definitions (the factor-to-variable rule is instantiated at the degree-2 pairwise factors that are the only kind occurring in this thesis's chain graphs; the marginalising integral becomes a finite sum). Three sanity lemmas PROVED, which are also concrete instances of thm:tree-exact: a leaf variable node sends the constant message 1 (empty product of the exclude-the-recipient rule); on a two-variable chain the single factor-to-variable message is the exact unnormalised marginal sum over x_1 of psi(x_0,x_1); and on a three-variable chain the belief at the middle node - the product of the forward and backward messages - equals the exact marginal sum over x_0, x_2 of psi_1 psi_2.
